In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best option for contact interaction searches at the Linear Collidor is to use polarized electron and unpolarized positron beams.
the polarization of the positron beam can improve the bounds on the contact-interaction parameters in the e + e − annihilation processes by a factor of two or more.
the polarization of both the electron and positron beam is the most powerful way to search for the four-fermi contact interaction at the Linear Collider.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to improve the contact-interaction limits, it is better to polarize both the electron and positron beam.
the polarization of the electron and positron beam at the Linear Collider will provide a more powerful probe of new physics than a polarized electron beam alone.
polarized e + e − beams provide the best means to probe contact interactions at a future Linear Collider.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization of the positron beam is crucial in order to improve the bounds on the contact-interaction parameters.
the sensitivity to contact interactions is significantly improved when the positron beam is polarized as compared to the case when only the electron beam is polarized.

, in general, the bounds obtained by polarizing the positron beam are stronger than the bounds obtained by only polarizing the electron beam, and in some cases the bounds obtained by simultaneously polarizing both the positron and the electron beams can be significantly stronger than the bounds from the two individual beam-polarization cases.
